Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to apply for the Backend Engineer, Payments Infrastructure role at Lattice Pay. For the past six years I have built payment services in Go and Java, most recently at Fernway, where I led the move of our ledger to an event-sourced design that cut reconciliation time from two days to four hours.

What draws me to your team is the focus on reliability at scale. I enjoy on-call work more than most people admit, and I have written the incident review template my current team still uses.

I would welcome the chance to talk about how I could help your team ship faster without losing sleep. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Kind regards,
Marta Ilunga
marta.ilunga@example.com

Hello Canopy team,

Please accept this letter as my application for the UX Designer position. I am a product designer with four years of experience in health and fintech apps, and I care most about research that changes what we build.

At Brightleaf Health I ran twelve rounds of usability tests on our appointment flow and redesigned it with the engineers; drop-off fell by a third. I am comfortable in Figma, I can prototype in code when it helps, and I like explaining design trade-offs to people who do not design.

I have attached my CV and a link to my portfolio. I would be glad to walk you through two case studies.

Warm regards,
Jonah Petrakis

To the hiring manager,

I saw your opening for a Senior Product Manager on the Checkout team and wanted to introduce myself. I have spent five years as a product manager on e-commerce platforms, the last two owning the payments page at Orchard Market.

My proudest result was a one-page checkout test that raised conversion by 4.1 percent across three million monthly visitors. I work closely with engineering and data science, and I write clear specs that people actually read.

I believe my background fits your goals for the coming year, and I would love to discuss them with you. My resume is attached.

Sincerely,
Priya Nandakumar

Dear recruiter,

My name is Tomas Reyes and I will graduate in May with a degree in Computer Science from Lakeshore State University. I am applying for your Software Engineer I opening.

During my internship at Bluefin Logistics I added retries and logging to a shipment tracking service, and I learned how much I enjoy making systems easier to run. In my capstone project my team of four built a study-group app used by 300 students.

I am eager to learn from experienced engineers and to contribute from day one. Thank you for considering my application; I look forward to hearing from you.

Best,
Tomas Reyes

How to Prepare for a Behavioral Interview in 2026

Behavioral interviews ask about your past to predict how you will work. Most companies use some version of the STAR method: situation, task, action, result.

Start by listing six to eight stories from your last few roles. Pick ones that show ownership, conflict handled well, a failure you learned from, and a result you can measure. Practice telling each in about two minutes.

Interviewers often probe: what exactly did you do, and how do you know it worked? Have numbers ready.

Finally, prepare two or three questions for the interviewer about the team and how success is measured.

Why Your Payment Service Needs Idempotency Keys

When a client retries a request after a timeout, your server may process the same payment twice. Idempotency keys fix this: the client sends a unique key with each logical operation, and the server stores the result under that key.

In this post we walk through a Postgres-backed implementation, the race conditions you must handle when two retries arrive at once, and how long to keep keys. We also cover what to return when a retry arrives while the first request is still running.

The pattern adds one table and about 200 lines of code, and it removes a whole class of incidents.

Tech Hiring Slows in Third Quarter, Survey Finds

Hiring for software roles slowed in the third quarter, according to a survey of 1,200 employers released on Tuesday. Openings for engineers fell 6 percent from the previous quarter, while demand for data and machine learning roles held steady.

Recruiters said candidates now face more interview rounds on average, and take-home assignments are returning at smaller companies. Salaries for senior engineers were flat.

Analysts expect hiring to pick up early next year as budgets reset.

From Teacher to Technical Program Manager: My Story

Three years ago I was teaching high school physics. Today I run hardware launches at a robotics company. People ask me how I made the switch, so here is what worked.

First, I learned to describe teaching in program terms: I planned a year of lessons for 150 students, managed dependencies between labs, and reported progress to parents and the principal.

Second, I took on a volunteer project managing a nonprofit's website rebuild. It gave me a real launch to talk about.

Third, I asked for informational interviews. Most people said yes.

Weeknight Lentil Soup (serves 4)

Ingredients
- 1 cup red lentils, rinsed
- 1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery stalks, chopped
- 3 cloves garlic
- 1 teaspoon cumin and 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
- 1 can chopped tomatoes
- 5 cups vegetable stock
- Juice of half a lemon

Method
Soften the onion, carrots and celery in olive oil for 8 minutes. Add garlic and spices for one minute. Add lentils, tomatoes and stock, simmer 25 minutes, then blend half. Finish with lemon and salt.
